content.text:
The Takeout import finished successfully, but it only contains a few days of data, and it did not connect your API account.

**Import status:** The job `job_1a742586f3e7` succeeded. It processed 9 of 9 files and inserted 11 records. Three files were skipped because they weren't in a supported format.

**Coverage:** The data covers only 1 to 3 October 2026.

| Source | Category / metric | Days with data |
|---|---|---|
| Fitbit Takeout | Steps (2 records) | 1 (Oct 1) |
| Fitbit Takeout | BMI | 1 (Oct 1) |
| Fitbit Takeout | Weight (unit unknown, so excluded from unit-converted summaries) | 1 (Oct 1) |
| Fitbit Takeout | Heart rate (1 sample) | 1 (Oct 1) |
| Fitbit Takeout | Resting heart rate | 1 (Oct 1) |
| Fitbit Takeout | Sleep: efficiency, minutes asleep, minutes awake, time in bed | 1 (Oct 2) |
| Google Takeout | Steps (1 record) | 1 (Oct 3) |

Categories such as exercise, nutrition, SpO2 and cardio fitness have no local records.

**Warnings and limitations:**
- Resting heart rate on 1 October had no estimate, so that day is treated as missing, not zero.
- A symbolic link in the archive was not extracted.
- Three files were not parsed: a sleep log CSV, an HTML file, and a JSON file with an unrecognized structure. They are kept on disk but not in the database.

**Does this connect your API account?** No. Takeout is a separate offline import. `connection_status` shows no verified API connection for either Google or Fitbit. To pull live data, I'd need to connect an account. Note that the legacy Fitbit Web API was scheduled to be turned off on 2026-10-30, so Google may be the more reliable option if you want API access.
